findings.title: Reschedule path cancels in SendGrid immediately, so the 100-pending-cancellation cap is still hit
findings.body: The PR exists because SendGrid keeps cancelled sends pending until their scheduled date and allows only 100 of them, after which new cancellations fail and the email goes out anyway. This call passes `immediateDelete=true`, which sends the SendGrid cancel straight away instead of just setting `cancelled=true` for the cron to process within the hour. Rescheduled bookings therefore keep consuming the capped pending-cancellation slots, and the bug is still reachable for reschedules. The same applies to the `true` argument in the workflow-delete and step-delete paths in workflows.tsx. In addition, the immediate path never deletes or marks the DB row. A later call on the same row (for example the `requestReschedule` flow followed by `handleNewBooking` on the already-cancelled booking) re-cancels the same batch_id in SendGrid, because reminders already flagged `cancelled` are not skipped.

findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and leaves reminders stuck
findings.body: The loop awaits a SendGrid cancel for each reminder, and the Prisma `delete` for each row is only executed afterwards by `Promise.all`. The whole loop sits in a single try/catch. If one `client.request` throws (bad batch_id, already-cancelled batch, rate limit), the loop exits and no rows are deleted, including those already cancelled in SendGrid. Every later cron run retries the same failing reminder first and can fail on it again, which blocks the other cancellations until the scheduled date passes. The next run may also re-cancel the batches that already succeeded. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete its row right after a successful cancel.

findings.title: Deletion is fire-and-forget, so the new `cancelled` flag may never be persisted
findings.body: The cancellation flow now depends entirely on a DB write (`cancelled: true`) made inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`. Every caller (handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx) invokes it without `await`, and the function swallows errors with `console.log`. On serverless deployments the request can finish before the update runs, and a failed update is silent. The email is then sent for a cancelled booking, which is the bug being fixed. The callers should await these calls, or the function should surface failures.

findings.title: No tests for the new cancellation flow
findings.body: The PR adds a DB column, a cron cancellation step and three different behaviours of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (no referenceId deletes the row, immediate SendGrid cancel, deferred flag). None are covered by tests, and the main conditions are untested: only reminders within the next hour are cancelled, rows are removed after cancel, and SendGrid errors are handled.
